enriched_description: Portable patient transport device consisting of a rectangular canvas or fabric sheet stretched taut between two parallel poles. Poles are typically metal (aluminum or steel) tubes approximately 2 meters long, extending beyond the fabric at both ends to serve as handles. Fabric is durable canvas or nylon in olive drab, orange, or white. Width approximately 50-60 cm. Some models have foldable legs for elevation. Wheeled variants (gurney) have a metal frame with 4-6 wheels and an adjustable height mechanism. Surface shows tension lines where fabric attaches to poles.

Upholstered convertible furniture piece functioning as both a sofa and a bed. Length approximately 1.8-2 meters, width 80-100 cm when closed. Seat cushion is thick and padded, covered in fabric or leather upholstery. Backrest is angled for sitting comfort. When converted, the frame unfolds to reveal a flat sleeping surface approximately 1.4m wide. Armrests may be present on one or both sides. Legs are short wooden or metal. Color varies widely (gray, beige, navy, brown). Mechanism hinges are visible along the seat edge when partially opened.

Dome-shaped Buddhist shrine with a hemispherical base (anda) rising from a square or circular platform. Dome is typically white-washed or stone-colored, smooth and rounded. Above the dome rises a square harmika (railing structure) topped by a tapering spire of stacked circular discs (chhatras). Base may have four cardinal gateways (toranas) with carved decorations. Overall height ranges from 3 meters to over 30 meters. Surface is smooth plaster or stone. Spire creates a distinctive stepped conical silhouette. Prayer flags may surround the structure.

Submersible warship with a streamlined cylindrical hull approximately 50-150 meters long. Hull is dark gray or black for underwater concealment. Prominent sail (conning tower) rises from the upper deck, housing periscopes and communications masts. Bow is rounded; stern tapers to a propeller shaft. Horizontal diving planes (fins) extend from the sides of the sail and stern. Torpedo tube openings visible at the bow. Surface shows riveted or welded steel plate construction. When surfaced, the deck is visible with various equipment and hatches. Nuclear subs have a characteristic bulge in the hull for the reactor.

Matching set of tailored garments consisting of a jacket and trousers (or skirt) made from the same fabric. Jacket features notched or peaked lapels, two or three front buttons, flap pockets, and a vent at the back. Trousers have a straight or tapered leg with a creased front. Fabric is typically wool, wool blend, or synthetic in solid colors (navy, charcoal, black, gray). Jacket shoulders are structured with padding. Lining is visible inside the jacket. Overall silhouette is formal and fitted. Shirt and tie are typically worn underneath.

Time-telling device consisting of a flat circular dial plate with hour lines radiating from a central point. A triangular or angled gnomon (shadow-casting blade) rises from the center, aligned to the local latitude. Dial plate is typically stone, metal, or wood with engraved or painted hour markings (Roman numerals or lines). Diameter 20-60 cm. Mounted on a pedestal or wall. Surface is weathered for outdoor use. Shadow cast by the gnomon indicates the time based on sun position. Ornamental sundials feature decorative borders and Latin inscriptions.

Single convex lens mounted in a frame, designed to concentrate sunlight. Lens is circular or oval, approximately 5-10 cm in diameter, made of glass or polished crystal. Frame is typically brass, wood, or metal with a handle or stand. Lens surface is smooth and transparent with a slight magnifying effect visible. When held in sunlight, it focuses rays to a bright pinpoint capable of igniting tinder. Historical versions have ornate metal frames; modern versions are simple magnifying lenses.

Eyewear with two tinted lenses mounted in a frame that rests on the nose and ears. Lenses are darkened (gray, brown, green, or mirrored) to reduce glare and UV exposure. Frame styles include aviator (teardrop lenses with thin metal frame), wayfarer (thick plastic frame with trapezoidal lenses), and wraparound (curved lenses extending to the temples). Bridge connects the two lenses over the nose. Temple arms extend back over the ears. Lens width approximately 50-60 mm per lens. Polarized lenses show a characteristic rainbow pattern when viewed at an angle.

Cream or lotion product packaged in a squeezable tube or pump bottle. Tube is typically 50-200 ml capacity, made of flexible plastic or aluminum laminate. Label displays SPF rating (15, 30, 50+) and UV protection information. Cap is a flip-top, screw-on, or pump dispenser. Product consistency is thick white or off-white cream that spreads smoothly on skin. Packaging features bright colors (yellow, orange, blue) with sun imagery. Squeeze tube has a flat crimped end. Pump bottles have a cylindrical body with a press-down nozzle.

Bridge structure characterized by a deck suspended from main cables that drape between two tall towers. Towers rise prominently above the deck, constructed from steel or concrete in an H-frame or A-frame shape. Main cables are thick braided steel bundles anchored at each end of the bridge. Vertical suspender cables hang from the main cables at regular intervals, supporting the deck. Deck is a flat roadway spanning the full length. Overall span can exceed 1 kilometer. Towers are typically painted gray or red. Cable pattern creates a distinctive catenary curve.
